channel.title: OpenFile Blog
channel.description: Guides, tips and notes on private, in-browser file tools.

item.title: Turn any document into Markdown for notes and AI chats
item.description: Why Markdown is worth it, how PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, email and notebooks are read in the browser, and how to deal with saved web pages and old Windows drawings.

item.title: Diagrams, charts and code pictures from plain text
item.description: Write a flowchart in three lines, paste a table for a chart, and turn code into a clean picture. Plus blobs, waves and printable graph paper, all in the browser.

item.title: From logo to G-code to turntable: 3D printing files in a browser
item.description: Turn a flat logo into a solid, read G-code layer by layer, film a spinning turntable video, and convert point clouds from scanners and drones.

item.title: Make flashcards, quizzes and worksheets that actually stick
item.description: Why spaced repetition and self testing beat rereading, how to turn notes into cards and quizzes, and the printables that save a teacher an evening.

item.title: robots.txt, sitemaps and redirects: the small files that steer search engines
item.description: What each file tells a crawler, the rules that trip people up, how to block AI crawlers, and how to move pages without losing traffic.

item.title: Calendar files and repeat rules, explained
item.description: What is inside an .ics file, how repeat rules like last Friday of the month work, and how to turn a spreadsheet or a shift pattern into calendar invites.

item.title: What is inside a FIT file from your watch
item.description: The binary format behind every Garmin, Wahoo and Coros workout, how to turn it into CSV or GPX, and how heart rate zones and training load are worked out.

item.title: OFX, QIF, CSV, CAMT and MT940: bank statement files explained
item.description: What each bank download format holds, which one to pick for a money app or a spreadsheet, and how to convert them without uploading your statement.

item.title: Scan receipts into a spreadsheet without uploading them
item.description: How on-device OCR reads a receipt photo, how the shop, date, tax and total are picked out, and tips for scans that come out right the first time.

item.title: Install OpenFile on any device, from a phone to a Linux box
item.description: Web app, Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iPhone: what each option gives you, how to install it, and which one I would pick for your device.

item.title: How OpenFile keeps your files private
item.description: What really happens when you drop a file into OpenFile, why nothing gets uploaded, and how you can check it yourself in two minutes.

item.title: How AI models run inside your browser tab
item.description: What happens when you press the button in the background remover, upscaler or transcriber: model downloads, workers, WebGPU and the WebAssembly safety net.

item.title: Ten PDF tips that save me time every week
item.description: Page ranges, smart compression, signing, OCR and the order I run things in. Small habits that make PDF work painless.

item.title: Shrink a PDF to fit an email limit
item.description: Gmail, Outlook and upload forms all have size caps. A practical routine to get under them: find the heavy part, pick the right preset, and split when you must.

item.title: Image compression explained, with a slider you can drag
item.description: Lossy, lossless, JPG, WebP and AVIF in plain words. Drag the slider to see what quality settings actually do to a picture.

item.title: HEIC, JPG, AVIF and JPEG XL compared
item.description: Four photo formats, what each one is good at, which browsers open them, and which I use for sharing, the web and my own archive. Test your browser live.

item.title: Editing video in a browser tab with WebAssembly
item.description: How ffmpeg runs inside your browser, why the first run downloads an engine, and how to get the best speed out of it.

item.title: Make a good GIF from a video clip
item.description: Why GIFs get huge, and the four settings that fix it: width, frame rate, length and colours. Includes a planner that estimates the size before you convert.

item.title: Building a batch pipeline for 200 product photos
item.description: A real walk through of the Workspace: resize, watermark, strip metadata, convert and zip, then save it as a recipe you can run again.

item.title: Fill and sign PDFs without uploading them
item.description: Form fields, signature images and certificate signatures explained, plus the order I fill, sign and flatten documents in, all inside the browser.

item.title: Sketch board tips: draw diagrams faster
item.description: Shortcuts, snapping, frames and export tricks for the Sketch board. Try the shortcut trainer right in the post.

item.title: EPUB, MOBI, PDF and comics: an ebook conversion guide
item.description: Reflowable versus fixed layout, which ebook format to keep, and how to convert, fix and read books on your device. With a live reflow demo.

item.title: A friendly guide to file formats
item.description: Which format to use for what, and what each one is good and bad at. Includes an interactive format explorer.

item.title: Opening DXF and CAD drawings in a browser
item.description: What a DXF file really contains, how to view layers and measure without AutoCAD, and how to turn a drawing into a PDF anyone can print.

item.title: The developer tools I reach for every day
item.description: JSON, JWT, regex, hashes, cURL and cron: a quick tour of the dev tools in OpenFile, with a live JSON formatter to play with.

item.title: Looking at your own CT and MRI scans, privately
item.description: What DICOM files are, why window and level matter so much, and how to view and share your scans without uploading medical data anywhere.

item.title: Text to speech that never leaves your device
item.description: How OpenFile reads text aloud with your system voices, and falls back to a small neural voice model that runs in the tab.

item.title: MIDI files explained, with a piano roll you can play
item.description: Why a MIDI file has no sound in it, what note numbers, velocity and channels mean, and how to play and render MIDI to MP3 or WAV in the browser.

item.title: CSV, JSON, Excel and Parquet: converting data without losing it
item.description: What each data format can and cannot hold, where conversions quietly break, and the tools I use to move data between them locally.

item.title: A practical guide to subtitles: SRT, VTT and ASS
item.description: The three subtitle formats you will meet, and how to fix the usual problems: wrong format, broken letters, drifting timing and missing tracks.
